findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Basic.lean:67 `theorem smul_left (a : R) (x y : M) : B (a • x) y = a * B x y`; :71 `theorem smul_right (a : R) (x y : M) : B x (a • y) = a * B x y`. Same convention in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean:105/115 (`inner_smul_left`/`inner_smul_right`) and in this repo at TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Hermitian.lean:136 (`complexAssociatedForm_smul_right : … v (z • w) = …`).
findings.fix: Swap the two names: `ω (a • x + b • y) y = a` becomes `apply_smul_add_smul_left` and `ω x (a • x + b • y) = b` becomes `apply_smul_add_smul_right`; update the three use sites at lines 203, 205, 245, 247 and the module docstring accordingly.
findings.issue: `apply_smul_add_smul_right` states `ω (a • x + b • y) y = a`, with the varying `smul_add_smul` argument in the *left* slot, and `apply_smul_add_smul_left` (line 120) states `ω x (a • x + b • y) = b`, with it in the *right* slot. The suffixes are inverted relative to the bilinear-form convention, so a reader who knows `BilinForm.smul_left` will pick the wrong lemma.

findings.evidence: Line 237-238 statement vs. line 137-138 statement; Mathlib names `Disjoint` arguments in order, e.g. Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Finite/Nondegenerate.lean:249 `lemma disjoint_rootSpan_ker_rootForm`.
findings.fix: Rename to `disjoint_span_pair_orthogonal` so the name lists the `Disjoint` arguments in statement order, and update the docstring list at line 52 and the use at line 298.
findings.issue: `disjoint_orthogonal_span_pair` proves `Disjoint (span ℝ {x, y}) (ω.orthogonal (span ℝ {x, y}))`, but names the second argument first — the opposite reading order from its sibling `disjoint_orthogonal_orthogonal` (line 136), whose first argument really is an `orthogonal`. The two names cannot both be parsed by the same rule.

summary: Two naming problems: the `_left`/`_right` suffixes on the hyperbolic-pair evaluation lemmas are swapped relative to the Mathlib bilinear-form convention the file builds on, and `disjoint_orthogonal_span_pair` lists its arguments in the reverse of its statement order. No notation is introduced; all other names describe their conclusions correctly.
